title: IN-FLIGHT ELECTRO-STATIC DISCHARGE MONITOR FOR SPACECRAFT - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop non-intrusive sensors for the characterization of Electro-Static Discharge on Spacecraft (e.g. for LEO constellations) together with an on-board events detection algorithm based on advanced approaches (e.g. AI based).Description: Electro-Static Discharge (ESD) phenomena on spacecraft have been estimated to contribute to around 20% to 25% of satellites anomalies overall.Yet, in-flight characterization of spacecraft ESDs in-flight has never been undertaken in a systematic way. In addition, while mitigation strategies are known for classical s/c configurations, new technologies (e.g. flexible solar arrays) require specific characterization in terms of risk (including in-flight) in order to demonstrate their maturity. The need for ensuring European space assetsresilience in LEO combined with the trend to mass product, fly and operate low power low mass constellation satellites calls for efficient and standardized environmental effects diagnostics, among which the one proposed here. The occurrence of ESDson Spacecraft in-flight depends on specific spacecraft electrical configurations and coupling with environments. LEO constellations growing market are subject to such risk as reported in the case of present constellations with thousands of events observed in flight (GEO (telecom, earth observation), MEO (navigation, orbit raising), as well as SSO polar environments also present a risk in that respect) due toboth surface and internal charging. From there, identifying relevant probing location on spacecraft systems where to systematicallyaccommodate non-intrusive /low resources sensors (e.g. current probes and well located RF receivers) would be of high interest to primes, spacecraft designers and agencies to improve our understanding of ESD phenomena in space and its relation to anomalies. In particular, the systematic integration of such sensors on low resource low mass constellation elements should enable large scale environmental effects diagnostics and improve the constellations resilience. This activity shall carry two phases in parallel or sequentially: Phase 1 - Review the state of the art in ESD detection and monitoring on spacecraft - Propose a concept design for a non-intrusive and system embedded method to detect, locate and measure arcing waveform signals onboard satellites - Perform breadboard testing to demonstrate critical functionalities - Define a consolidated design for an ESD monitor - Define a way forward to reach a TRL of 6 Phase 2 - Assess available methodologies (including AI/ML based) and propose a concept design for an on-board events detection algorithm - Develop a breadboard model to simulate events detection and test the detection method - Consolidate the design and propose a detailed design - Establish a development roadmap.http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

На основание чл. 67, ал. 5 от ЗОП възложителят може да изиска от участниците по всяко време да представят всички или част от посочените в чл. 58, ал. 1 от ЗОП документи, когато това е необходимо за законосъобразното провеждане на процедурата. Отговор „не“ се отнася за всички обстоятелства. При отговор „да“ лицето трябва да посочи конкретното обстоятелство, както и евентуално предприетите мерки за надеждност. title: EnVision Spacecraft Independent Software Verification and Validation (ISVV)
description:
EnVision is a Venus orbiter mission selected by ESA’s Science Programme Committee as the fifth Medium-class mission in the Agency’s Cosmic Vision plan. It will be the first mission to investigate Venus from its inner core to its upper atmosphere, characterising the interaction between its atmosphere, surface/subsurface and interior. It aims at providing a holistic view of Venus, studying the planet’s history, activity, and climate. An overview of the EnVision mission and its objectives can be found on the Agency website here: https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/EnVision_factsheet.
Thales Alenia Space Italia (TAS-I) is issuing this ITT as EnVision Prime Contractor, and conducting the procurement under the principles of ESA Best Practices for the selection of subcontractors. TAS-I will release an Invitation To Tender for the procurement of the Independent Software Verification and Validation (ISVV).
Independent Software Verification and Validation (ISVV) is an engineering practice intended to improve quality and to reduce development risks of the On-board Software.
The main objective of ISVV activities is to find issues that would really provoke a mission loss, severe mission degradation or major non-compliance to requirements.

This objective will be reached by performing the following main tasks:
•	independently verify the SW components subject of this ISVV contract
•	independently analyze the specifications, the design and justification documents, the source code and test results
•	identifying critical areas

title: DEVELOPMENT OF IN-SITU REAL-TIME SENSOR FOR MOLECULAR CONTAMINATION MONITORING OF FLIGHT HARDWARE - EXPRO PLUS
description: The number of future missions with higher and higher cleanliness requirements is constantlyincreasing (e.g. LISA, AEOLUS-2). Current monitoring methods for molecular contamination do onlyallow a limited representativeness with regards to the actual levels deposited on sensitive surfaces.Indeed, molecular contamination witnesses can almost never be placed close enough to the sensitive surfaces (for accessibility precautionary reasons) and cannot provide constant monitoring due to the incompatibility with some of the testing environments. Besides, measurements are performed periodically in laboratory environment and only provide punctual values, typically on monthly basis. For all these reasons, contamination measurements can only be taken as estimateand hypotheses are needed inorder to evaluate the levels on sensitive surfaces. This situationbecomes critical for highly sensitive items and clearly the morestringent are the requirements, thehigher risks are undertaken.Having the capability to perform in-situ real-time monitoring of the molecular contaminationdeposited on sensitive surfaces will allow to determine the actual contamination levels and to identify which phases are the most critical. Such a technology will contribute to ensure that the instrument performance will be met and will provide the capability to quickly implement mitigation actions if contamination levels increase unexpectedly. In addition, the use of this technology can be extended in flight. Operation in-flight will allow the optimization of the commissioning anddecontamination phases, thus ensuring optimal performances while maximizing instrumentavailability during the mission.Currently, two technologies are considered for the development of such a sensor, either based onOptical Micro-Electro-Mechanical-System or on micro-wave transduction.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Design definition considering the operational constraints- Manufacturingof breadboard to experimentally assess the suitability of the selected technology and its robustness against typical environment- Definition of a test plan and implementation of the associated test campaign laboratoryenvironment to determine the evaluated system performance- Identification of the required steps to manufacture a qualification unit for in-flight operationProcurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. description: La Mini Piattaforma spaziaLe ad Alta TecNOlogia “PLATiNO” ha la finalità di sviluppare la leadership dell’industria italiana nell’ambito delle piccole piattaforme modulari multimissione: obiettivo primario è la definizione e lo sviluppo delle tecnologie Nazionali abilitanti le future missioni dell’ASI attraverso l’identificazione di una piattaforma standard “multi-purpose”, in grado quindi di imbarcare tutta una gamma di P/L scientifici e applicativi per missioni Near Earth. Allo scopo di consolidare la capacità della piattaforma e assicurarne la sua flessibilità, è stato previsto l’utilizzo della piattaforma multipurpose PLATiNO per altre due missioni con payload ottico ad alta risoluzione (HR) e payload iperspettrale compatto (HYP) e l’avvio dell’associata Roadmap Tecnologica Ottica, avente lo scopo di garantire la realizzazione di strumentazione per future missioni ottiche di Osservazione della Terra. ASI vuole procedere all’affidamento delle attività volte ad avviare sviluppi tecnologici necessari alla realizzazione della roadmap ottica attraverso attività a differente livello di maturità tecnologica, garantendo da un lato l’avvio di progetti innovativi a basso TRL, dall’altro consolidando le capacità nazionali attraverso attività a medio-alto TRL. La scadenza del bando è stata prorogata al 12 maggio 2023 ore 12.00 (vedere comunicazioni in calce). La scadenza per la richiesta di chiarimenti è stata prorogata al 28 aprile 2023, ore 12.00.
